artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $\mathbb{F}_p = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. For any function $f : \mathbb{F}_p \to \mathbb{C}$, define its Fourier transform by
$$\widehat{f}(z) := \sum_{u \in \mathbb{F}_p} f(u)\, e^{2\pi i u z / p}, \qquad z \in \mathbb{F}_p.$$
Fix $\varepsilon \in (0,1]$ and constants $A, B > 0$. Decide whether the following statement holds for all sufficiently large primes $p$:

Suppose $f, g : \mathbb{F}_p \to [0,1]$ satisfy
$$\widehat{f}(0) = \widehat{g}(0) > \frac{p}{(\log p)^A}$$
and
$$\max_{z \in \mathbb{F}_p} \bigl|\widehat{f}(z) - \widehat{g}(z)\bigr| < p \exp\!\bigl(-\sqrt{\log p}\bigr).$$
Then for every function $h : \mathbb{F}_p \to [0,1]$ with $h(u) \le f(u)$ for all $u \in \mathbb{F}_p$ and $\widehat{h}(0) \ge \varepsilon\, \widehat{f}(0)$, there exists a function $h' : \mathbb{F}_p \to [0,1]$ such that $h'(u) \le g(u)$ for all $u \in \mathbb{F}_p$ and
$$\max_{z \in \mathbb{F}_p} \bigl|\widehat{h'}(z) - \widehat{h}(z)\bigr| < \frac{p}{(\log p)^B}.$$

(In the hypothesis, $\exp(-\sqrt{\log p})$ may be replaced by any function that decays to $0$ faster than every negative power of $\log p$.)
